about: MUTATING — delete the forge registry's image versions that no train, no rollback and no cluster can want any more (infra/forge/prune-registry-versions.sh <mode> [keep_trains]). Backlog 9789a827, David 2026-09-17 (the replacement disk was not delivered; 'that order sounds great' — buy the headroom). Measured 2026-09-16: /opt/forgejo/data is 93 GB of the forge's 228 GB disk — the container registry every train pushes a boss:<sha> image to (1–3 GB each, plus boss-ci:<sha> per train) — and nothing pruned the REGISTRY side: prune-registry-tags.lib.sh removes LOCAL docker tags only after the registry holds them (the registry is the rollback path), disk-floor-sweep stops at its floor, and the registry grows ~2 GB per train. Measured 2026-09-17: 1,423 container versions; docker push stores a tag (its one file is the OCI index) plus two untagged sha256 children where the layers live, so the script reads EVERY tag's index through /v2 before classifying and deletes a child only when every tag referencing it goes. THE KEEP SET IS DERIVED, and a half that cannot be derived is a refusal that deletes nothing: the live images (every owner image the cluster runs; deploy/boss in namespace boss required — the watchdog's own read), the rollback target (the converge's last-built stamp the watchdog rolls to by name), the last N landed trains' shas (landed-train-shas.lib.sh over the newest 2N pr-train packets; keep_trains, default 10), latest, everything newer than 24 h, and everything unclassifiable (a tag that is not a sha, an unreadable index, every orphan while any index was unreadable). THE CREDENTIAL is the converge's own docker login for the registry host (the checkout owner's ~/.docker/config.json), used as Basic on the packages API and as a bearer minted at /v2/token for the manifest reads; it rides in a curl config file, never argv, and is never printed. A 403 refuses NAMING THE SCOPE the forge asks for — read:package on the listing, write:package on the first DELETE — a ceremony for David, and the real run stops on that first DELETE. --dry-run derives the keep set, reads the registry and prints the plan (would DELETE / unclassified, by name) and the record; --for-real DELETEs tags first, then children, judged by HTTP code (204 gone, 404 already gone, anything else stops with the count so far on the record), and prints each planned version with its OUTCOME as the verb — DELETED / GONE / FAILED <code> / KEPT — never would DELETE (backlog ea67ad87: the first real run, ops-request 973beaa2, 2026-09-17, printed the plan file as-is and appended the outcomes after the runner's 100 KB cut, so the packet read 898 conditionals under an OK verdict). The record is ONE JSON line: kept/delete/deleted/unclassified per package, the keep halves, listed versus the forge's total, and df of the data directory before and after — bytes are not claimed because the packages API declares no sizes and Forgejo's [cron.cleanup_packages] frees the blobs later (measured on that first real run: 1,337 deleted, df moved 724 KB); its cadence is not in this tree, so the record's cleanup_cron carries SCHEDULE and OLDER_THAN read off the forge's own app.ini under the data directory, or says the file could not be read; read df on the packet after that cron has run. The record and the verdict line come BEFORE the per-version list (backlog 5323f3ef, 2026-09-17: 1,313 lines and the record last, cut off by the runner's 100 KB window), and the full list is /var/backups/boss/registry-prune/<stamp>.txt on the forge, named in the record as list_file. Own timeout: one listing page per 50 versions, one manifest read per tag, one DELETE per version. The switch-instance-database shape and process: an explicit per-verb authorization, a precedent for the PROCESS, not a loosened default.
